                On periodic subgroups of factorized groups

                                                   By
                         NILVANA FRANCIOSI and FRANCESCO DE GIOVANNI



   1. Introduction. Let the group G = A B be the product of two subgroups A and B. If
N is a normal subgroup of G, the f a c t o r i z e r of N in G is the subgroup X (N) = A N n B N .
It is easy to show that X ( N ) has the triple factorization

              X ( N ) = (A n B N ) ( B n A N ) =    (A n B N ) N = (B n A N ) N .

Thus the investigation concerning factorized groups very often leads to the consideration
of groups with a triple factorization of the form

              G=AB=AK=BK,

where K is a normal subgroup of G. It has recently been proved by Robinson and
Stonehewer [6] that if the factors A, B and K are abelian, then the group G has a central
series. However, an example of Sysak [7] shows that such a group G is not always locally
nilpotent, even if K has rank 1.
   The aim of this article is to study the behaviour of elements of finite order in groups
with a triple factorization by locally nilpotent subgroups. An arbitrary periodic locally
soluble group G = A B = A K = B K , factorized by three locally nilpotent subgroups
A, B and K, with K normal in G, need not be locally nilpotent, since Sysak [7] has
constructed a group of this type, where K is an infinite minimal normal subgroup of G.
On the other hand Amberg [1] proved that G is locally nilpotent, provided that A and
B are hypercentral. Improving this theorem, we shall prove that every periodic group
G = A B = A K = B K factorized by three locally nilpotent subgroups A, B and K, with
K normal in G, is locally nilpotent if one of the factors A and B is hyperabelian. This will
be a consequence of results on groups having a triple factorization by subgroups with
normal Sylow re-subgroups for a fixed set ~ of primes.
   In the general case, information are obtained on the structure of periodic subgroups
of groups with a locally nilpotent triple factorization. In fact, it will be proved that if
the hyperabelian group G = A B = A K = B K is the product of two locally nilpotent
subgroups A and B and a nilpotent normal subgroup K, then every periodic normal
subgroup of G is locally nilpotent. This can be used to show that the set of all elements
of finite order of G is a locally nilpotent subgroup, provided that either G is locally
polycyclic or G is soluble and one of the factors A and B has finite torsion-free rank.
314                             S. FRANCIOSI a n d E DE GIOVANNI                      ARCH. MATH.

  O~(G) is the m a x i m u m periodic n o r m a l n-subgroup of G, for a set n of primes,
  n' is the complementary set of primes to n.
  A group G has finite torsion-free rank if it has a series of finite length whose factors are
  either periodic or infinite cyclic.
  A subgroup H of a factorized group G = A B is called factorized if A n B __<H
  and H = (A n H) (B c~ H). Thus H is a factorized subgroup if and only if X ( H ) = H.

   2. Statements and proofs. Let n be a set of primes. A group G is called n-dosed if the
set of all n-elements of G is a subgroup. In particular, if p is a prime, a group G is p-closed
if and only if it has a unique Sylow p-subgroup. Thus a locally finite group is locally
nilpotent if and only if it is p-closed for each prime p. If the group G contains a n-closed
normal subgroup N such that G/N has no non-trivial n-elements, it is clear that G is
n-closed. Moreover, if the group G is n-closed and N is a periodic n o r m a l subgroup of
G, the factor group GIN is also n-closed.
   In order to study products of n-closed groups, the following result of Zaicev [8] is
needed (see also [4], L e m m a 4.6A).

  Lemma 1. Let the group G = A B be the product of two subgroups A and B, and let Ao
and B o be normal subgroups of A and B, respectively. I f A locally satisfies the maximal
condition on subgroups and x = ab (a e A, b e B) is an element of G normalizing the
subgroup H = ( A o, Bo), then a normalizes Z (H) n Ao.

  Lemma 2. Let n be a set of primes, and let the group G = A B = A K = B K be the
product of two n-closed subgroups A and B, and a normal subgroup K such that A n K and
B n K are periodic and n(K) n n is empty. I f A locally satisfies the maximal condition on
subgroups and Ao is a periodic abelian normal n-subgroup of A such that A~ is locally finite,
then A o is normal in G and is contained in B.

   P r o o f. As B is n-closed, the set B 1 of all n-elements of B is a n o r m a l subgroup of B.
Then B 1 K is n o r m a l in G = BK, and the factor group G/B~ K ~ B/B~ (B n K) has no
n-elements, so that A o is contained in B~ K. Since A o K is normal in G = AKi the
subgroup Bo = Ao K n B~ is normal in B. M o r e o v e r A o K = A o K n B 1 K = B o K, with
A o n K = B o n K = 1, and hence Bo ~ Ao is abetian. The subgroup H = ffAo, Bo) is
contained in Ao K = Bo K, and so H = Ao (H n K) = B o (H c~ K), where H ~ K is n o r m a l
in H.
   Let a o be an element of A o of order a power of a prime q, a n d write ao = bo h, with bo
in B o and h in H n K. Then ( a o ) and ( b o ) are Sylow q-subgroups of ( a o ) ( H c~ K )

belongs to Ao n Bo < Z(H). In particular a~ is in Z ( H ) n Ao. O n the other hand, a

  We can now prove the following result on groups with a triple factorization by n-closed
subgroups.

   Theorem 3. Let n be a set of primes, and let the group G = A B = A K = B K be the
product of three n-closed subgroups A, B and K, where K is a locally finite normal sub-
group of G. I f one of the factors A and B is hyperabelian and locally polycyclic, then G
is n-closed.
   P r o o f. It is clearly enough to show that the factor group G/On(G) is n-closed, so that
we may suppose On (G) = 1. In particular the n-closed locally finite normal subgroup K
of G is a n'-group. Assume that A is hyperabelian and locally polycyclic. It follows from
Lemma 2 that A has no non-trivial abelian normal n-subgroups, so that n (A) n n = 0, as
A is n-closed. Then also the factor group G/K ~- A/(A c~ K ) has no n-elements, so that
n(G) n n = 0, and G is n-closed.        []

  The previous theorem has the following consequences.

   Corollary 4. Let n be a set of primes, and let the locally finite group G = A B
= A K = B K be the product of three n-closed subgroups A, B and K, where K is normal
in G. I f one of the factors A and B is hyperabelian, then G is n-closed.

   Corollary 5. Let the group G = A B = A K = B K be the product of three locally nilpo-
tent subgroups A, B and K, where K is a periodic normal subgroup of G. I f one of the factors
A and B is hyperabelian, then the set of all elements of finite order of G is a locally nilpotent
subgroup. In particular, if G is periodic, it is locally nilpotent.
  Corollary 5 can be used to obtain the following property of metanilpotent products of
periodic locally nilpotent groups. This was already known in the case of a product of two
periodic abelian groups (see [2]).

   Corollary 6. Let the metanilpotent group G = A B be the product of two periodic locally
nilpotent subgroups A and B. Then the Hirsch-Plotkin radical of G is a factorized subgroup.
  P r o o f. It is well-known that the group G is periodic (see [4], Theorem 3.2.6). Let H
be the Hirsch-Plotkin radical of G. The factorizer X = X (H) of H in G has the triple
factorization
                X = A'B* = A*H = B'H,
where A* = A n B H and B* = B n A H , and hence it is locally nilpotent by Corollary 5.
As the factor group G/H is nilpotent, the subgroup X is subnormal in G, so that X < H.
Thus X = H, and H is a factorized subgroup of G.       []

  In the above results the assumption that the normal subgroup K is periodic was used
to produce large periodic normal subgroups. N o w we investigate the behaviour of
316                              S. FRANCIOSI and F. DE GIOVANNI                        ARCH; MATH.


elements of finite order in a triply factorized group G = A B = A K = B K , when the
normal subgroup K is not periodic.


   Proposition 7. Let the hyperabelian group G = A B = A K = B K be the product o f two
locally nilpotent subgroups A and B, and a nilpotent normal subgroup K. Then every
periodic normal subgroup o f G is locally nilpotent.

   P r o o f. Let T be the maximum periodic normal subgroup of G. If the result holds
for the factor group G'K'. then T K ' 'K' is locally nilpotent, so that T K K ' is locally
nilpotent, and hence also T < T K is locally nilpotent Thus we may suppose that K is
abelian. As locally finite residually locally nilpotent groups are locally nilpotent, it is
enough to show that T/Op, (G) is locally nilpotent for each prime p. Hence without loss
of generality it can be assumed that Op, (G) = 1 for some prime p, so thal in particular
  (K) _ { p}.
   Suppose first that A n K and B c~ K both are periodic. Let A o be a periodic abelian
normal p'-subgroup of A which is contained in TK. The normal subgroup T K of G is
periodic-by-abelian, so that T is the set of all elements of finite order of TK. Thus A o < T,
and so AoG < T is locally finite. Application of Lemma 2 yields that A o is normal in G. and
hence A o - 1. Therefore A 1 = A c~ T K does not contain periodic abelian non-trivial
A-invariant p'-subgroups. As A t ~ K and A 1/(A 1 c~ K ) ~ A ~ K / K are periodic, it follows
that also the normal subgroup A~ of A is periodic, so that A 1 is a p-group. Moreover
T K = A K c~ T K = AI K, and hence T / ( T c~ K ) ~ T K / K = A 1 K / K is a p-group. There-
fore T is a p-group, and so it is locally nilpotent.
   In the general case. the subgroups A n K and B c~K both are normal in
G = A K = B K , so that also N = ( A n K) (B n K) is a normal subgroup of G. It follows
from the first part of the proof that the maximum periodic normal subgroup To/N of the
factor group G / N is locally nilpotent. Let E be a finite subgroup of T There exists a
finitely generated subgroup E~ of A such that E < E1 K. Then L = ( E n A ~ K, E l ) is
a finitely generated subgroup of A, and hence xs nilpotent, so that E c~ A n K < Z, (L}
for some positive integer n. As K is abelian, it follows that E c ~ A n K < Z , [ L K ) ,
and thus E c ~ A n K < Z n ( E ) .     If G * = G / ( A r , K), the same argument shows
that E * n B * ~ K * < Z , , ( E * ) for some positive integer m. On the other hand,
E*/(E* n B* n K*} ~ E* (B* n K*)/(B* c~ K*) is isomorphic to the finite subgroup
E N N of To~N, so that E * / ( E * n B * c ~ K * I            is nilpotent. Therefore E* =
E f A n K)/(A c~ K ) ~ E/(E c~ A c~ KI is nilpotent, and hence also E is nilpotent. This
proves that T is locally nilpotent.       []


   Our last two results show that in certain cases the set of all elements of finite order of
the triply factorized group G is a subgroup.


   Theorem 8. Let the soluble group G = A B = A K = B K be the product o f two locally
nilpotent subgroups A and B, and a nilpotent normal subgroup K. I f one o f the factors A
and B has finite torsion-free rank, then the set o f all elements o f finite order o f G is a locally
nilpotent subgroup.
Vol. 61, 1993               Periodic subgroups of factorized groups                          317

   P r o o f. Assume that A has finite torsion-free rank, and let T be the subgroup
generated by all elements of finite order of G. If T K ' / K ' is periodic, it follows from
Proposition 7 that T K ' / K ' is locally nilpotent. Thus T K / K ' is locally nilpotent, so that
TK is locally nilpotent, and hence the subgroup T is periodic and locally nilpotent.
Therefore it is enough to show that the set of all elements of finite order of the factor
group G/K' is a subgroup, and in particular we may suppose that K is abelian. Then
B n K is a normal subgroup of G = BK, and B/(B n K) -~ A/(A n K) has finite torsion-
free rank. Put G = G/(B n K). The locally nilpotent group A is periodic-by-nilpotent (see
[5] Part 2, Theorem 6.36), and hence it has a series of finite length with central or periodic
factors. Then it follows from Theorem 4.6.1 of [4] that the factorized group G = A B has
finite torsion-free rank. If V is the maximum periodic normal subgroup of G, the factor
group G/V has finite Prfifer rank (see [5] Part 2, Lemma 9.34). Then G/V is locally
nilpotent by Theorem B of [3], and hence is torsion-free, so that the subgroup V is the
set of all elements of finite order of G. Let E be the subgroup generated by a finite set of
elements of finite order of G, and let E 1 be a finitely generated subgroup of B such that
E < E I K . As E / ( E n B n K ) ~ - E ( B n K ) / ( B n K ) is finite, the subgroup E n B n K is
finitely generated, and hence L = ( E n B c~ K, E l ) is a finitely generated subgroup of B.
Thus L is nilpotent and E n B n K < Z n (L) for some positive integer n. Since K is abelian,
we have also that E c~ B n K is contained in Zn(LK), and so E n B n K < Z,(E). There-
fore E/Z,(E) is finite, and E is finite-by-nilpotent (see [5] Part 1, Corollary 2 to Theo-
rem 4.21). Then E is finite, and the set of all elements of finite order of G is a sub-
group.      []

  Theorem 9. Let the hyperabelian group G = A B = A K = B K be the product of two
locally nilpotent subgroups A and B, and a nilpotent normal subgroup K. I f G is locally
polycyclic, then the set of all elements of finite order G is a locally nilpotent subgroup.
   P r o o f. As in the proof of Theorem 8 we may suppose that the subgroup K is abelian,
and it is enough to show that the set of all elements of finite order of G is a subgroup.
   Suppose first that A n K = B n K = 1, and without loss of generality assume that the
abelian normal subgroup K of G is torsion-free. Let A o be an abelian normal p-subgroup
of A, where p is a prime, and suppose that A o is not contained in B. Let a be an element
of Ao\B, and write a = bx, with b in B and x in K \ { I } . Let q be a prime such that q 4: p,
and put L = x G and M = (xq) ~. Assume that x belongs to M. Then there exists a finitely
generated subgroup H of G such that x is in V = (xq) ~. Hence x q belongs to V q, and so
V q = V. The subgroup ( x q, H ) is finitely generated, and hence polycyclic, so that
V < ( x q, H ) n K is a finitely generated torsion-free abelian group, a contradiction since
V q = V. Therefore x is not in M, and L / M is a non-trivial abelian group of exponent q.
Write G = G/M, and let )~ be the factorizer of L = L / M in the factorized group G = A B.
Then
